verses.1: And it happened that when Jesus finished teaching his twelve disciples, he left to teach and preach in the cities around them.
verses.2: And when John heard about the preparations for the crucifixion, he sent his disciples to take care of those matters.
verses.3: He said to him, “Are you indeed the one who is coming, or do we expect someone else?”
verses.4: And when Jesus spoke, he said to them, “Go and tell John what you hear and see.”
verses.5: The blind will see again, and the deaf will hear. The sick will be healed, and the poor will be blessed. The dead will rise, and the poor will be saved.
verses.6: And it is better if he does not fall into my hands.
verses.7: After these words, Jesus began to speak to the crowd about John. “Why have you come into the wilderness to be tempted by the wind?” he asked.
verses.8: But why did you come here to see me? To see a man who is trapped in a situation of poverty. Those who pay taxes in the palaces of kings are indeed those who live in poverty.
verses.9: But why have you come here? To see a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more importantly, a prophet.
verses.10: This is about what is written there. Now, I will send my messenger before you, so that he can prepare the path ahead for you.
verses.11: I say to you, there are no women greater than John the Baptist among his descendants. But the younger one is greater in the kingdom of heaven than he is.
verses.12: But from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven is being attacked. And they are attacking it and taking away what belongs to it.
verses.13: For all the prophets and the law, they prophesied until John came.
verses.14: And if you want to stand by, then that person is Elyas, who will come soon.
verses.15: He who has such ears, listen carefully.
verses.16: In what way can I compare this with other situations? It’s the same as when children sit in the markets, bargaining with each other for things they want.
verses.17: They say: “We have wept for you, but you did not cry out. We have been grieved, but you did not stop.”
verses.18: For John came, neither eating nor drinking. They say that he has demons in him.
verses.19: The son of man came, eating and drinking. They said, “Look! This is a man who loves to eat and drink; he is also a friend of sinners.” And wisdom was given to him through his actions.
verses.20: Then he began to glory in those cities where his greatest forces were located. He knew that they wouldn’t be deceived by him.
verses.21: Do not worry, Chorazin; do not worry, Bethsaida. For even if those forces that appeared in Tyre and Sidon were once insignificant and insignificant, they still became important over time.
verses.22: I tell you that Tyrus and Sidon will be more affected by this day of judgment than you will.
verses.23: And you, Kafarnauum, will not rise until you reach the heavens. You will descend to the depths of darkness. For if those forces that occurred in Sodomi were indeed possible in your case, then they would still be possible today.
verses.24: I also tell you that in the day of judgment, it will be more important for Sodomon to be accepted than for you.
verses.25: In that time, Jesus replied, “I confess to you, Father in heaven and on earth, that I have hidden these things from the wise and sensible, and revealed them to children.”
verses.26: Oh, Father, it was such a blessing that this happened before you.
verses.27: It has always been given to me by my father. No one knows the son unless it’s the father himself; nor does anyone know the father unless it’s the son. And if the son wants to reveal something, then he can do so.
verses.28: Now, let all those who are being cut and baptized come to me, and I will rest your minds.
verses.29: Therefore, take my burden upon yourselves and learn from me that I am also humble in my heart. And you will find relief for your souls.
verses.30: For my load is useful, and my burden is light.
